name: Alabama
tagline: From Cheaha Mountain and Little River Canyon to Black Belt prairie and Mobile Bay.
intro: Alabama's byways climb Lookout Mountain and the Talladega range in the northeast and run south through the old cotton country of the Black Belt to the Gulf forts at Mobile Bay. This chapter follows the Alabama Scenic Byways Program, set up by the Alabama the Beautiful Act of 2000 with a Designating Committee and a Scenic Byways Advisory Council, and supported by an ALDOT state byway coordinator. Its list of eleven mixes four national byways with seven state ones, and three of the national roads, the Natchez Trace among them, were first designated in the 1990s by the Legislature and the Governor before the program existed.

programs.label: Alabama Scenic Byways
programs.issuer: Alabama Scenic Byways Designating Committee and Advisory Council

members.name: Alabama's Coastal Connection
members.blurb: A 130-mile run along Alabama's Gulf shore that crosses the mouth of Mobile Bay by auto ferry between the brick forts Gaines and Morgan, with shrimp boats at Bayou La Batre and dunes at Bon Secour.

members.name: The Appalachian Highlands Scenic Byway
members.blurb: About eighty miles of Highway 9 and its neighbors from Heflin to Fort Payne, through the Talladega National Forest and the cotton fields around Centre, then up Lookout Mountain past Little River Canyon.

members.name: Barbour County Governors' Trail
members.blurb: About 36 miles of state highway from Clio through Louisville and Clayton to Eufaula, in a county that gave Alabama six governors, George and Lurleen Wallace among them, ending at the Shorter Mansion.

members.name: The Black Belt Nature and Heritage Trail
members.blurb: Loop drives through thirteen counties of dark soil that once grew the region's cotton, past Gaineswood, a Demopolis mansion eighteen years in the building, and on to fried catfish at Ezell's Fish Camp.

members.name: Black Warrior River Scenic Byway
members.blurb: A twelve-mile town loop on both banks of the Black Warrior at Tuscaloosa and Northport, over three bridges and past riverwalks and the site where Alabama kept its capitol from 1826 to 1847.
members.note: No route line: the national dataset does not include this road and the state publishes no map line for it.

members.name: Leeds Stagecoach Route
members.blurb: An old Indian trail turned stagecoach road through Leeds and the Little Cahaba valley, past horse farms and marked old houses, near the railroad tunnel where local tradition sets John Henry's race with the steam drill.
members.note: Shown on the map as Alabama's Stagecoach Route Through Leeds.

members.name: Lookout Mountain Parkway
members.blurb: Alabama's share of a three-state road along Lookout Mountain from Gadsden toward Chattanooga, by Little River Canyon and DeSoto State Park, and each August lined with tables for the World's Longest Yard Sale.

members.name: The Natchez Trace Parkway
members.blurb: The parkway's 33 Alabama miles cross the state's northwest corner, climbing to Freedom Hills Overlook and crossing the Tennessee River at Colbert Ferry, where the Chickasaw George Colbert ran a ferry and inn from 1800 to 1819.

members.name: Selma to Montgomery Historic Trail
members.blurb: US 80 from the Edmund Pettus Bridge in Selma through the low hills of Lowndes County to the Capitol in Montgomery, the 54 miles walked in the voting rights march of March 1965.

members.name: Talladega Scenic Drive
members.blurb: State Route 281 leaves US 78 west of Heflin and follows the crest of the Talladega Mountains past Cheaha, at 2,407 feet the top of Alabama, until the pavement gives out at Adams Gap.

members.name: Tensaw Parkway
members.blurb: Highways 225 and 59 skirt the east edge of the Mobile-Tensaw Delta, with fourteen boat landings into its creeks and swamps, the old town site at Blakeley State Park and the Fort Mims memorial.
members.note: No route line: the national dataset does not include this road and the state publishes no map line for it.
